subject: Behavioral Economics
title: The Rise of Nudge Units
description: One-minute skill: The Rise of Nudge Units.

hook.text: In 2010, the UK created a team to improve government policy using nudges. It paid for itself in its first year.

buildup.text: The Behavioural Insights Team, nicknamed the 'Nudge Unit,' redesigned tax letters, health forms, and energy bills.

discovery.text: A single line change in tax letters — 'most people in your area pay on time' — increased on-time payments by 15%.

twist.text: Over 200 governments now run nudge units. A $50 letter redesign can collect millions more in taxes.

climax.text: Nudge units prove that small, cheap changes in design can outperform expensive mandates and enforcement.

quiz.question: What did the UK's Nudge Unit achieve with tax letters?
options: Adding a social norm message increased on-time payments by 15%

details.summary: Nudge units are government teams dedicated to applying behavioral insights to public policy. Starting with the UK Behavioural Insights Team in 2010, over 200 nudge units now operate worldwide, testing behavioral interventions through randomized controlled trials to improve policy outcomes.
details.whyItMatters: Nudge units represent the institutionalization of behavioral economics in government. They have demonstrated that low-cost behavioral interventions can improve tax collection, health outcomes, and program uptake while rigorous testing ensures they.
takeaways: Over 200 government nudge units operate worldwide as of recent counts
The UK Behavioural Insights Team was the first and most influential nudge unit
Rigorous randomized controlled trials distinguish nudge units from intuition-based policy

faq.question: What has the UK Behavioural Insights Team accomplished?
faq.answer: They have increased tax collection by millions through better letter design, improved organ donation registration through website nudges, increased pension enrollment through defaults, and tested hundreds of interventions. They helped launch similar units worldwide.

faq.question: Why do nudge units use randomized controlled trials?
faq.answer: Because intuitions about what works are often wrong. Testing interventions on random groups before and after provides causal evidence. Many interventions that seem promising fail when tested, and some that seem trivial produce large effects. Data replaces guesswork.
